newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to change securities and bank laws.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to change securities and bank laws.

text.p: The Hungarian government has approved new draft legislation for securities and financial institutions and for their supervision, government spokesman Elemer Kissa said on Thursday.
Speaking after a weekly cabinet meeting, he told a news conference the draft legislation was aimed at protecting investors.

If it is approved by parliament, banks would be allowed to trade in government securities from January 1, 1997. Trade in what a press release called "riskier securities" would be permitted from January 1, 1999, at latest.

The draft sets or increases capital requirements for all institutions trading in securities. Securities houses allowed to do business on commission only would need a minimum 20 million forints capital.

Securities houses allowed to trade also on their own account would require capitalisation of 100 million forints, while investment companies involved also in lending would need a minimum one billion forints capital.
Existing companies would have to increase their capital to meet the above requirements by December 31, 1997.

The minimum capital requirement for banks would be two billion forints, cooperative banks would need 100 million forints and companies providing financial services would be required to have a minimum 20 million forints capital.
Existing banks would have to meet the new requirement by December 31, 1998, and cooperative banks by December 1, 2001.

The money and capital markets would be supervised by the State Money and Capital Markets Supervision, which is to be set up by merging the State Banking Supervision and the State Securities and Exchange Supervision.
